226.h: Babcock University is a private university in Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, owned by the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 1999, the year the first private universities in Nigeria were licensed, which makes it one of the country's oldest private universities. Church life is part of the campus, with a university church, chaplaincy and weekly worship programmes.
226.a: Babcock offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees across a wide range of subjects. It runs its own teaching hospital, Babcock University Teaching Hospital, where medical and health students train, and a university press.
226.c: Students live in halls of residence on campus at Ilishan-Remo, a town in the Remo area of Ogun State, between Lagos and Ibadan.

227.h: Bauchi State University, now named Sa'adu Zungur University (SAZU), is a public university owned by the Bauchi State Government. The National Universities Commission lists 2011 as its year of establishment. The university was renamed in honour of Sa'adu Zungur, a Bauchi-born writer and pioneer of Northern Nigerian politics.
227.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes for students from Bauchi State and the wider north-east.
227.c: Its main campus is at Gadau, with further campuses at Misau and in Bauchi city.

228.h: Bayero University Kano (BUK) is a federal university in Kano, the largest city in northern Nigeria. It grew out of Bayero University College, which was attached to Ahmadu Bello University, and it became a full university in 1975. It was the first university in Kano State. It is named after Abdullahi Bayero, a former Emir of Kano.
228.a: BUK is one of the major universities of north-western Nigeria and offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, law, engineering, sciences and Arabic and Islamic studies.
228.c: The university is in Kano, the capital of Kano State.

229.h: Baze University is a private university in Abuja, established in 2011. It was founded by Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed.
229.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
229.c: The campus is in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

230.h: Bells University of Technology, also called Bellstech, was the first private university of technology in Nigeria. It was established in 2004 and admitted its first students in the 2005/2006 academic session, which is the date the National Universities Commission records.
230.a: As a university of technology, Bells concentrates on engineering, the sciences, technology and related management programmes.
230.c: The university is located in Ota, Ogun State, close to the Lagos border.

231.h: Benson Idahosa University (BIU) is a private Christian university in Benin City, Edo State, established in 2002. It was first called Christian Faith University and was renamed after Archbishop Benson Idahosa, the Pentecostal minister from Benin City who founded it and served as its first president. Its president today is his son, Bishop Faith Emmanuel Benson Idahosa of the Church of God Mission.
231.a: BIU is accredited by the National Universities Commission and offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, with a Christian ethos that reflects its founder's evangelical beliefs.
231.c: The university is in Benin City, the capital of Edo State.

232.h: Benue State University was established in 1992 as a public university owned by the Benue State Government. In 2025 it was renamed Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi (MOAUM), after the Catholic priest who served as governor of Benue State in the early 1990s and founded the university.
232.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, with more than 58 graduate programmes across nine colleges and faculties, and is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
232.c: It is located in Makurdi, the capital of Benue State, on the River Benue.

233.h: Bingham University is a private university founded in 2005 and owned by the Evangelical Church Winning All (ECWA). Lectures began in 2006, and the university moved to its permanent campus on 3 March 2008. By 2024 it had graduated more than 7,000 students.
233.a: Bingham offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across 12 faculties. Its teaching hospital, where medical students train, is in Jos, Plateau State.
233.c: The permanent campus is in New Karu, Nasarawa State, about 26 kilometres from Abuja, which makes it easy to reach from the capital.

234.h: Kashim Ibrahim University, Maiduguri, formerly Borno State University, is a public university owned by the Borno State Government. It was established in 2016, with Professor Umar Kyari Sandabe as its pioneer vice-chancellor. President Muhammadu Buhari inaugurated its senate building in June 2021. In January 2025 Governor Babagana Zulum approved its new name, which honours Sir Kashim Ibrahim, the first governor of Northern Nigeria.
234.a: The university is organised into five faculties with more than 20 departments.
234.c: It is located in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State in north-eastern Nigeria.

235.h: Bowen University is a private Baptist university affiliated with the Nigerian Baptist Convention. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2001. It is named after Thomas Jefferson Bowen, an American Baptist missionary who worked in Yoruba land in the nineteenth century.
235.a: Bowen offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and health sciences, within a Christian ethos.
235.c: The university is located at Iwo in Osun State, south-western Nigeria.

236.h: Caritas University is a private Catholic university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2005.
236.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
236.c: Its campus is at Amorji-Nike, in Enugu State, south-eastern Nigeria.

237.h: Chrisland University is a private university founded in 2015 and accredited by the National Universities Commission. It was established by the proprietors of the Chrisland group of schools.
237.c: It is located in Abeokuta, the capital of Ogun State.

238.h: Christopher University is a private university founded in 2015 and recognised by the National Universities Commission.
238.c: It is located in Mowe, Ogun State, on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway corridor.

239.h: Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University (COOU), formerly Anambra State University, is a public university owned by the Anambra State Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2000. It is named after Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu, the former military governor of the Eastern Region.
239.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
239.c: The university has a campus at Uli and its permanent site at Igbariam, in Anambra East local government area in the north of Anambra State.

240.h: Confluence University of Science and Technology (CUSTECH) is a public technical university owned by the Kogi State Government. The National Universities Commission lists 2020 as its year of establishment. Its name refers to Kogi State's position at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers.
240.a: The university concentrates on science and technology programmes. In 2024 the National Universities Commission gave full approval to all its courses.
240.c: The campus is at Osara in Kogi State.

241.h: Covenant University (CU) is a private Pentecostal Christian university founded by the Living Faith Church Worldwide. It received its operating licence from the Federal Government in February 2002 and admitted its first students later that year. The university is built around the idea of developing the 'total man', combining academic study with personal, spiritual and leadership development.
241.a: Covenant University offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in engineering, sciences, business, social sciences and the humanities, and it is regularly ranked among the leading private universities in Nigeria.
241.c: The campus is at Canaanland in Ota, Ogun State, near the Lagos border.

242.h: Crawford University is a private Christian university owned by the Apostolic Faith Mission. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2005.
242.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
242.c: It is located in Igbesa, Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.

243.h: Crescent University is a private university founded by Prince Bola Ajibola, a Nigerian judge and former Attorney General of the Federation, under the Islamic Mission for Africa. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2005.
243.a: The university is organised into colleges: the Bola Ajibola College of Law, and colleges of environmental sciences; information and communication technology; natural and applied sciences; arts, social and management sciences; and health sciences.
243.c: It is located in Abeokuta, the capital of Ogun State.

245.h: Delta State University, Abraka, known as DELSU, is a public university owned by the Delta State Government. It was founded on 28 April 1992. The institution has a long history on its Abraka site: it began as a government teacher training college that offered Grade II teaching certificates before independence in 1960, later became a college of education, and was then upgraded to a university.
245.a: DELSU offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes for students from Delta State and across Nigeria.
245.c: The main campus is at Abraka in Delta State, in the Niger Delta region.

246.h: Delta State University of Science and Technology, Ozoro, now known as Southern Delta University (SDU), is a public university owned by the Delta State Government. The National Universities Commission lists 2021 as its year of establishment.
246.a: SDU offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses in eleven faculties: Administration and Management, Agriculture, Arts, Basic Medical Sciences, Communication and Media Studies, Computing, Engineering, Environmental Science, Law, Science, and Social Sciences.
246.c: The university is located in Ozoro, Delta State.

247.h: Dominican University, Ibadan is a private Catholic university run by the Order of Preachers, better known as the Dominicans. It is the order's first university in Africa. The Dominican Order was founded by the Spanish priest Dominic de Guzman in 1216 and has been involved in university education for more than 800 years. The National Universities Commission records the Ibadan university's establishment in 2016.
247.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
247.c: It is located in Ibadan, Oyo State.

248.h: Ebonyi State University, Abakaliki (EBSU) is a public university owned by the Ebonyi State Government. Accounts give 1999 for its founding and the National Universities Commission records 2000. Its medical faculty is older than the university itself: it began in 1991 as the Faculty of Health Sciences of Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT).
248.a: EBSU's medical school is accredited by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria to train medical students and resident doctors. Its main teaching hospital grew from the Abakaliki Specialist Hospital, which was originally set up to respond to an outbreak of Guinea worm disease in the area.
248.c: The university is in Abakaliki, the capital of Ebonyi State.
